title: Ready for Theatre

patient.name: Mr Lee Chin Huat
patient.presenting_complaint: Admitted to the day ward for left eye cataract surgery; here for the pre-operative assessment

history.hpc: Mr Lee is in the day ward for left eye cataract surgery under local anaesthesia. He says: 'Today my turn to do the cataract operation, nurse say need to check me first before go in.' The OT must complete the dayward pre-operative assessment, confirming the key details and recording vital signs.
history.pmhx: Left cataract (for surgery). Type 2 diabetes, hypertension — both controlled.
medications: Amlodipine 5mg OD (taken with a sip of water as advised)
history.social_hx: Lives with wife who is waiting outside. Fasted as instructed.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Left cataract; eye marked for surgery per protocol

investigations.dayward_preop_assessment: Pre-operative assessment completed using the DISM framework — Diagnosis (left cataract), Indication for surgery (visually significant cataract), Surgery planned (phacoemulsification with IOL, left eye), Medical conditions (diabetes, hypertension — controlled). Anaesthesia type: local. Eye to be operated: LEFT (confirmed and marked). Vital signs recorded; fasting and medication instructions verified.
investigations.vital_signs: BP, pulse, and (if required) blood sugar documented within acceptable ranges.

diagnosis: A complete, correct dayward pre-operative assessment for left eye cataract surgery using the DISM framework, with the correct eye confirmed/marked, anaesthesia type noted, and vitals and fasting status checked. The OT competency is thorough, accurate pre-op documentation and safety checks; the surgery is the surgeon's.

immediate: Complete the DISM assessment: Diagnosis, Indication, Surgery planned, Medical conditions
Confirm and document the anaesthesia type (local) and the correct eye (LEFT), checking it is marked
Record vital signs and confirm fasting status and which medications were withheld/taken
Check for relevant issues (e.g., diabetes control, blood thinners) and flag any abnormal result
Document everything clearly and ensure the notes accompany the patient to theatre
Escalate any abnormal vitals or unclear consent/eye-marking before the patient proceeds
follow_up: Surgeon/nurse to proceed once the assessment and safety checks are complete
Ensure documentation accompanies the patient into theatre
Hand over any flagged issues (e.g., glucose) to the nurse/doctor
patient_education: Reassure him the checks are routine safety steps before surgery
Confirm with him which eye is being operated as part of the safety check
Explain what to expect next (going into theatre, local anaesthesia)
Answer simple questions and defer surgical details to the surgeon

key_points: Confirms the planned surgery and the operative eye with the patient
Verifies fasting status and which medications were withheld or taken
Explains the pre-op checks to the patient
Completes the DISM framework (Diagnosis, Indication, Surgery, Medical conditions)
Documents anaesthesia type and confirms/checks the correct marked eye
Records vital signs and notes any out-of-range results
Documents clearly so notes accompany the patient to theatre
Understands the purpose of a structured pre-op assessment for safety
Recognises correct-eye confirmation/marking as a critical safety step
Knows abnormal vitals or unclear marking must be escalated before surgery
Knows the OT role is assessment/documentation, not the surgery
Completes and documents the full DISM assessment accurately
Escalates any abnormal result or safety concern before the patient proceeds
Ensures documentation accompanies the patient to theatre
Reassures the patient and confirms the operative eye with them
